name: Zendesk
task: A help desk, tickets or a shared inbox
summary: Customer service suite: ticketing, messaging, voice, help centre and AI agents.
best_for: support teams past the point where a shared inbox works, who need routing, a help centre and reporting in one place and have the volume to justify per-agent pricing
skip_if: you are a small team handling support out of email. The entry tier is email and ticketing only, the features people buy Zendesk for start at $55 a seat, and the Copilot AI is not available below $115. Also skip it if your case volume is low enough that per-resolution AI metering is more admin than benefit
honest_knock: Three separate multipliers sit on top of the number you first see. The prices shown are annual-billed: month-to-month costs more: €25, €69 and €149 per agent against €19, €55 and €115, read from the Netherlands on 7 October 2026. Copilot, the AI the product is currently sold on, is a $50 per-agent add-on that their own page restricts to Professional and higher: the $19 and $55 tiers cannot have it at any price, and on the $115 Professional seat it is a 43% uplift. And the AI agents that are included are metered by automated resolutions: past the allowance you pay per resolution, so the bill moves with how well the AI works rather than with how many people you hire. App Builder, Action Builder and Voice are metered on consumption alongside it. Price the tier you need with the add-ons you actually want switched on, because the $19 entry and a working configuration are far apart.

pricing.entry_price_terms: per agent a month, annual billing (US storefront)
pricing.notes: (re-verified 2026-08-12, read on their own pricing page from two countries) Per agent per month on annual billing, US storefront: Support Team $19, Suite Team $55, Suite Professional $115. Suite Enterprise + Copilot is quote-only. The page geo-prices — read from Europe the same three tiers show €19, €55 and €115 — so check which storefront your quote came from. Annual billing carries a stated 20% discount. Read again from the Netherlands on 7 October 2026: the euro tiers are unchanged, and the page now also prints monthly rates of €25, €69 and €149 per agent (a saving of 24%, 20% and 23% on annual), includes 5 automated resolutions per agent a month on the Team tiers and 10 on Professional, and charges €1.50 per extra resolution committed or €2.00 pay-as-you-go. Paid add-ons on top of the seat price: Copilot $50 per agent/month (€50), Workforce Engagement bundle $50 (€50), Contact Center $83 (€82). Copilot can be attached to Professional and higher only. AI agents are included in Suite and Support plans but metered by 'automated resolutions' beyond the plan allowance, and App Builder, Action Builder and Voice are billed on consumption above their own allowances.

exit_test.what: On 13 November 2026 the supplied session tested Zendesk Suite Professional trial setup, AI questions and billing-ticket routing. Admin copilot created Billing on the first attempt. Trigger creation succeeded only after the third approval: subject was rejected, then title, then subject_includes_word was used according to the session note. The final assistant summary described routing newly created tickets when the subject contains factuur or invoice to Billing. A synthetic ticket titled Vraag over mijn factuur van oktober was saved as Ticket #3 using an internal note, without a public reply; its assignee field displayed Billing. Only the Dutch factuur branch was tested; the invoice branch, later tickets and departmental reporting were not tested. With Dutch account language, the English question received Ik spreek uw taal niet. The Dutch question received an answer distinguishing dated hands-on reviews from supplier-research reviews. The tester found that consistent with the site; no independent source-completeness or general accuracy benchmark was performed. Setup ingested the site; no categorised kit import was performed.
exit_test.awkward: Trigger creation required three approvals; the English AI question was refused in the Dutch-language account. Cross-language behaviour after configuration changes is unknown.

sessions.what: On 13 November 2026 we tested Zendesk Suite Professional on its trial, using our own site as the knowledge source. We built a Billing group and a routing trigger with the admin copilot, saved one synthetic invoice ticket, and asked the AI agent a Dutch and an English question. We did not open checkout, and we did not test support, invitations, roles, API access, export or cancellation.
findings: Daan created the account the day before and we did not see that step. In the accelerated setup the website address came prefilled, and about 35 seconds later the AI agent had read our site. The setup asked for no card, no phone number and no mailbox connection. An optional banner offered an expert call.
The trial runs on Suite Professional with 12 of 14 days left when we looked. The trial therefore includes features that the entry plan Support Team does not.

The admin copilot created the Billing group on the first approval. The routing trigger took three approvals: the copilot first used the field subject, which Zendesk rejected, then title, then subject_includes_word. The whole job took about 1.5 minutes.

We then saved a synthetic ticket titled 'Vraag over mijn factuur van oktober' as an internal note, with no public reply. The assignee field showed Billing (Ticket #3). Only this Dutch 'factuur' branch was tested. We did not test the 'invoice' branch or reporting per department.
The plan page lists the admin copilot under Suite Professional. We did not test the same trigger on Suite Team, where it would be set up by hand.

The AI agent runs in Dutch because the account language is Dutch. Our English question was refused with 'Ik spreek uw taal niet'. A Dutch question about whether we test software ourselves got an answer in about 10 seconds that matches our site: some reviews are tested hands-on and dated, others are supplier-research reviews. This is one answer, not an accuracy benchmark.

The plan page in the trial shows, per agent per month in euros: Support Team 19 billed annually or 25 monthly, Suite Team 55 or 69, and Suite Professional 115 or 149. The annual option is labelled 24% off. Copilot is a separate add-on at 50 euros per agent per month. A recommendation popup suggested Suite Team and also listed Suite Growth, which the full comparison did not.
We opened no checkout, so tax, totals, minimums and renewal terms are unknown. These euro prices are not directly comparable with the dollar price read on the US page on 7 October 2026.
not_tested: Checkout, tax, minimums and renewal terms
Support, invitations, roles and API access
The 'invoice' keyword branch and reporting per department
The same routing on Suite Team without the copilot
sessions.note: Findings as written up after the session; no pass/fail per task was scored.

open_questions.question: Can a non-admin agent's dashboard be limited to their own performance numbers?
Can a customer cancel at any time, and what happens to an annual plan that is cancelled mid-term?
Which data can a customer export, in which formats, on which plans?
Where is customer data stored, and can a customer choose the region?
Which plans can be bought month to month, and at what price?

Our price check could not put a number on this part of the cost: Paid add-ons (Copilot, Workforce Engagement, Contact Center) and AI agents, App Builder, Action Builder and Voice beyond their allowances are charged on top and are not in these totals. Can you publish the price or the rule?
